tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

input.description: Read both skill files

content.content:
---
name: startup
description: >-
  Start of day, or sitting down at either machine: sync this machine against GitHub,
  then report where the last session left off and wait. Use when Eric says '/startup',
  'good morning', 'starting up', 'where did I leave off', 'what was I working on',
  'picking this back up', or opens a session without naming a task. Do not use for the
  end-of-session sign-off (use closeout).
---

# Startup

The front door for a work session on either machine. This skill owns no logic of its own — it runs `dev-sync`, whose Step 5 loads context back in.

## What to do

Invoke the `dev-sync` skill and run it end to end, Step 0 through Step 5.

Do not reimplement any of it here. If the sync behaviour or the context report needs to change, change `dev-sync/SKILL.md`. One home for the procedure, and this file is an alias so the command matches how Eric actually thinks about it: "sync" is what the machine does, "startup" is what he is doing.

## After the report

`dev-sync` Step 5 ends with a short "picking up" report and a stop. Hold there and wait for Eric to confirm or redirect. Do not begin the next task on your own — `docs/STATUS.md` records where the last session stopped, which is not the same as what he wants to do this morning.

If he names a repo when he invokes this, pass it through so Step 5 reports on that one instead of guessing from the most recent commit.

## Not this

- Not the morning brief. Calendar, email and the shape of the day belong to the `morning` / `morning-briefing` work. This skill answers "where was I", not "what's my day".
- Not a memory loader. Global memory arrives through the SessionStart hook before this runs; do not re-read `USER.md` or `MEMORY.md` by hand.
=====
---
name: closeout
description: >-
  End-of-session sign-off ritual. Sweeps loose ends, commits and pushes what needs it,
  verifies memory capture, writes a cross-harness handoff, and reports "clear to sign
  off" or what's still open. Use when the user says "/closeout", "any loose ends?", "am
  I good to sign off?", "close out for the night", "closing out", "goodnight", "wrap up
  for the day", or asks for a system health check before leaving. Do not use at the
  start of a session (use startup) or for a standalone automation health check (use
  claude-stack-doctor).
---

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".

content.text:
Nothing covers this across repos yet. You were right to ask.

**What startup does today.** `/startup` hands off to `dev-sync` Step 5, which reads just one repo: the one you name, or else the active repo with the most recent commit. It reads that repo's STATUS.md and newest handoff, then prints a "Blocked on:" line. After a day spread over several repos, that means one repo's decisions show up and the rest stay hidden. `where-was-i.py` does look at every repo, but it only prints the first `## Next` line, not open questions.

**My recommendation: list open decisions, not handoffs.** Closeout already writes the questions waiting on you into each repo's `## Open questions` in STATUS.md. A list of handoff files would only give you file names to open. The change would be:

1. Add a `--decisions` flag to `where-was-i.py`. It would list the real Open questions from every repo whose STATUS changed in the last N days, skipping blank, "ANSWERED" and "None" entries. Below that, it would name any handoffs written since then, as pointers only.
2. Add one line to `dev-sync` Step 5 that runs it, so the startup report gets a "Decisions waiting on you" section covering every repo.

There's one weak spot. Closeout sometimes writes a pointer instead of the question itself. NCAA_BestPractices_Doc's entry, for example, just says "See PLAN.md 'Questions for the Chris meeting'". It's worth tightening closeout so the questions are written out in STATUS.md.

**What tomorrow's startup would miss right now** (open questions from STATUS files updated in the last 2 days):
- **NCAA_BestPractices_Doc:** the Chris-meeting questions in `PLAN.md` and SOURCES.md § F.
- **project-triage:** confirm how "Laurel Proulx" is spelled (WomensHealth_Survey).
- **CATES:** the white paper's ROI and cost figures have no source. Verify them or label them as illustrative before anyone sees them.
- **Flint:** whether the Verkhoshansky entry should stay `untested` (your call), and confirming the D-I two-a-day preseason rule.
- **KeystoneOS:** turn off the GPS step in Windows `Refresh_All_Data`, delete 3 old GPS copies by hand, and move the backup manifest off OneDrive.
- **PlayerProfiles_FB:** whether the 9/1–3/28 reporting window should roll forward.
- **MatchupAnalysis_FB2026:** what the `(M)/(B)/(O)` codes mean, and whether PFF charts blocking for FCS games.

Several of these are weeks old and only came up because yesterday's sweep touched every repo. The new flag would treat them the same way, which is probably what you want.

I haven't changed anything. If you want it, I'll add the flag, the Step 5 line and the closeout tightening. That work goes in the `~/.claude/scripts` and `~/.claude/skills` repos.

"""Where was I? One line per project: the first item under `## Next` in docs/STATUS.md.

Sorted by when STATUS.md was last committed, newest first. Flags repos with
uncommitted or unpushed work, since those are the ones a closeout missed.

Usage:
    python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py            # last 14 days
    python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --days 60
    python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --all
"""
import argparse
import glob
import os
import re
import subprocess
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DEV = os.path.expanduser("~/Desktop/DEV") if os.name == "nt" else os.path.expanduser("~/DEV")


def git(repo, *args):
    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    return r.stdout.strip()


def first_next(path):
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    m = re.search(r"^## Next\s*\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", text, re.M | re.S)
    if not m:
        return "(no ## Next section)"
    parts = []
    for line in m.group(1).splitlines():
        s = line.strip()
        if not parts:
            s = re.sub(r"^(\d+[.)]|[-*])\s*", "", s)
            if re.search(r"\w", s) and not s.startswith(("#", "```", "|")):
                parts.append(s)
        elif not s or re.match(r"^(\d+[.)]|[-*])\s", s) or s.startswith("#"):
            break
        else:
            parts.append(s)
    if not parts:
        return "(## Next is empty)"
    item = " ".join(parts)
    return item[:160] + ("…" if len(item) > 160 else "")


def inspect(status_path):
    repo = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(status_path))
    when = git(repo, "log", "-1", "--format=%cs", "--", "docs/STATUS.md") or "uncommitted"
    flags = []
    status = git(repo, "status", "-sb", "--porcelain").splitlines()
    if len(status) > 1:
        flags.append("DIRTY")
    if status and "ahead" in status[0]:
        flags.append("UNPUSHED")
    return os.path.relpath(repo, DEV), when, first_next(status_path), flags


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=14)
    ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    paths = glob.glob(os.path.join(DEV, "*", "docs", "STATUS.md")) + \
        glob.glob(os.path.join(DEV, "*", "*", "docs", "STATUS.md"))
    paths = [p for p in paths if "_ARCHIVE" not in p and "worktrees" not in p]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
        rows = list(ex.map(inspect, paths))

    cutoff = (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=a.days)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    rows = [r for r in rows if a.all or r[1] == "uncommitted" or r[1] >= cutoff]
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[1], reverse=True)

    print(f"Where was I — {len(rows)} projects" + ("" if a.all else f" touched in the last {a.days} days"))
    for name, when, nxt, flags in rows:
        flag = f"  [{' '.join(flags)}]" if flags else ""
        print(f"\n{when}  {name}{flag}\n    NEXT: {nxt}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

action.description: "keep" leaves the worktree and branch on disk; "remove" deletes both.

discard_changes.description: Required true when action is "remove" and the worktree has uncommitted files or unmerged commits. The tool will refuse and list them otherwise.
